source_text: Ἔτι δὲ καὶ περὶ τοῦ ναοῦ ἐρῶ ὑμῖν, ὡς πλανώμενοι οἱ ταλαίπωροι εἰς τὴν οἰκοδομὴν ἤλπισαν, καὶ οὐκ ἐπὶ τὸν θεὸν αὐτῶν τὸν ποιήσαντα αὐτούς, ὡς ὄντα οἶκον θεοῦ. σχεδὸν γὰρ ὡς τὰ ἔθνη ἀφιέρωσαν αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ ναῷ. ἀλλὰ πῶς λέγει κύριος καταργῶν αὐτόν, μάθετε: Τίς ἐμέτρησεν τὸν οὐρανὸν σπιθαμῇ ἢ τὴν γῆν δρακί; οὐκ ἐγώ; λέγει κύριος: Ὁ οὐρανός μοι θρόνος, ἡ δὲ γῆ ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν μου: ποῖον οἶκον οἰκοδομήσετέ μοι, ἢ τίς τόπος τῆς καταπαύσεώς μου; ἐγνώκατε, ὅτι ματαία ἡ ἐλπὶς αὐτῶν. πέρας γέ τοι πάλιν λέγει: Ἰδού, οἱ καθελόντες τὸν ναὸν τοῦτον αὐτοὶ αὐτὸν οἰκοδομήσουσιν. γίνεται, διὰ γὰρ τὸ πολεμεῖν αὐτοὺς καθῃρέθη ὑπὸ τῶν ἐχθρῶν: νῦν καὶ αὐτοὶ οἱ τῶν ἐχθρῶν ὑπηρέται ἀνοικοδομήσουσιν αὐτόν. πάλιν ὡς ἔμελλεν ἡ πόλις καὶ ὁ ναὸς καὶ ὁ λαὸς Ἰσραὴλ παραδίδοσθαι, ἐφανερώθη. λέγει γὰρ ἡ γραφή: Καὶ ἔσται ἐπ’ ἐσχάτων τῶν ἡμερῶν, καὶ παραδώσει κύριος τὰ πρόβατα τῆς νομῆς καὶ τὴν μάνδραν καὶ τὸν πύργον αὐτῶν εἰς καταφθοράν. καὶ ἐγένετο καθ̓ ἃ ἐλάλησεν κύριος. ζητήσωμεν δέ, εἰ ἔστιν ναὸς θεοῦ. ἔστιν, ὅπου αὐτὸς λέγει ποιεῖν καὶ καταρτίζειν. γέγραπται γάρ: Καὶ ἔσται, τῆς ἑβδομάδος συντελουμένης οἰκοδομηθήσεται ναὸς θεοῦ ἐνδόξως ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι κυρίου. εὑρίσκω οὖν, ὅτι ἔστιν ναός. πῶς οὖν οἰκοδομηθήσεται ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι κυρίου, μάθετε. πρὸ τοῦ ἡμᾶς πιστεῦσαι τῷ θεῷ ἦν ἡμῶν τὸ κατοικητήριον τῆς καρδίας φθαρτὸν καὶ ἀσθενές, ὡς ἀληθῶς οἰκοδομητὸς ναὸς διὰ χειρός, ὅτι ἦν πλήρης μὲν εἰδωλολατρείας καὶ ἦν οἶκος δαιμονίων διὰ τὸ ποιεῖν, ὅσα ἦν ἐναντία τῷ θεῷ, Οἰκοδομηθήσεται δὲ ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι κυρίου. προσέχετε δέ, ἵνα ὁ ναὸς τοῦ κυρίου ἐνδόξως οἰκοδομηθῇ. πῶς, μάθετε. λαβόντες τὴν ἄφεσιν τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν καὶ ἐλπίσαντες ἐπὶ τὸ ὄνομα ἐγενόμεθα καινοί, πάλιν ἐξ ἀρχῆς κτιζόμενοι: διὸ ἐν τῷ κατοικητηρίῳ ἡμῶν ἀληθῶς ὁ θεὸς κατοικεῖ ἐν ἡμῖν. πῶς; ὁ λόγος αὐτοῦ τῆς πίστεως, ἡ κλῆσις αὐτοῦ τῆς ἐπαγγελίας, ἡ σοφία τῶν δικαιωμάτων, αἱ ἐντολαὶ τῆς διδαχῆς, αὐτὸς ἐν ἡμῖν προφητεύων, αὐτὸς ἐν ἡμῖν κατοικῶν, τοὺς τῷ θανάτῳ δεδουλωμένους ἀνοίγων ἡμῖν τὴν θύραν τοῦ ναοῦ, ὅ ἐστιν στόμα, μετάνοιαν διδοὺς ἡμῖν, εἰσάγει εἰς τὸν ἄφθαρτον ναόν. ὁ γὰρ ποθῶν σωθῆναι βλέπει οὐκ εἰς τὸν ἄνθρωπον, ἀλλ’ εἰς τὸν ἐν αὐτῷ κατοικοῦντα καὶ λαλοῦντα, ἐπ’ αὐτῷ ἐκπλησσόμενος, ἐπὶ τῷ μηδέποτε μήτε τοῦ λέγοντος τὰ ῥήματα ἀκηκοέναι ἐκ τοῦ στόματος μήτε αὐτός ποτε ἐπιτεθυμηκέναι ἀκούειν. τοῦτό ἐστιν πνευματικὸς ναὸς οἰκοδομούμενος τῷ κυρίῳ.
pass_a_gloss: And yet I will also speak to you about the temple, how the wretched ones, being deceived, have hoped in the building, and not in their God who made them, as being the house of God. For they have dedicated it in the temple almost as the nations do. But how does the Lord speak, abolishing it, learn: Who has measured the heaven with a span or the earth with a handful; not I, says the Lord: The heaven is my throne, and the earth is the footstool of my feet: what kind of house will you build for me, or what is the place of my rest? You have known that their hope is vain. And again he says: Behold, those who have torn down this temple, they themselves will build it. It happens, for because they wage war, it was destroyed by the enemies: now they, the servants of the enemies, will rebuild it. Again, as the city and the temple and the people of Israel were about to be delivered, it was revealed. For the scripture says: And it will be in the last days, and the Lord will deliver the sheep of the pasture and the fold and their tower into destruction. And it happened as the Lord spoke. Let us seek if there is a temple of God. There is, where he himself says to make and prepare. For it is written: And it will be, when the week is completed, the temple of God will be built gloriously in the name of the Lord. I find, then, that there is a temple. How, then, will it be built in the name of the Lord, learn. Before we believed in God, our heart's dwelling was perishable and weak, as truly a temple built by hand, because it was full of idolatry and was a house of demons, because we did what was contrary to God. But it will be built in the name of the Lord. Pay attention, then, that the temple of the Lord may be built gloriously. How, learn. Having taken the forgiveness of sins and having hoped in his name, we became new, being created again from the beginning: therefore, in our dwelling, God truly dwells in us. How? His word of faith, his calling of promise, the wisdom of righteousness, the commandments of teaching, he himself prophesying in us, he himself dwelling in us, opening for us the door of the temple, which is the mouth, giving us repentance, leading us into the imperishable temple. For the one who desires to be saved looks not at the man, but at the one dwelling and speaking in him, being amazed at him, because neither has he ever heard the words spoken from his mouth, nor has he himself ever desired to hear. This is the spiritual temple being built for the Lord.

pass_b_english: I must also speak to you about the temple. The wretched were deceived and pinned their hopes on a building instead of on the God who made them, as if that building were God's house. They dedicated it almost the way the nations do. So learn how the Lord speaks against it: 'Who measured the heavens with a span or the earth with a handful? Was it not I?' says the Lord. 'Heaven is my throne, and the earth is the footstool for my feet. What kind of house will you build for me, or what place will serve as my resting place?' (Isaiah 66:1-2). You have recognized that their hope is empty. Again he says: 'Look, those who tore down this temple will themselves rebuild it.' This happened because they waged war, so enemies destroyed the temple; now even the enemies' own servants will rebuild it. Once more, when the city, the temple, and the people of Israel were about to be handed over, this was revealed. For Scripture says: 'In the last days the Lord will deliver the sheep of the pasture, their fold, and their tower to destruction' (Micah 4:12). And it happened just as the Lord said. So let us ask whether there is a temple of God. There is—where he himself says to make and prepare it. For it is written: 'When the week is completed, the temple of God will be built gloriously in the name of the Lord.' I conclude, then, that a temple exists. Learn how it will be built in the Lord's name. Before we believed in God, the dwelling of our hearts was perishable and weak—truly a hand-built temple—because it was full of idolatry and was a house of demons, since we did everything contrary to God. But it will be built in the name of the Lord. Pay attention, then, so that the Lord's temple may be built gloriously. Learn how. We received forgiveness of sins and hoped in his name, and we became new, created again from the beginning; therefore God truly dwells in us, in our inner dwelling. How? His word of faith, his calling of promise, the wisdom of his righteous judgments, the commandments of his teaching—he himself prophesying in us, he himself dwelling in us—opens for us the door of the temple, which is the mouth, giving us repentance and leading us into the imperishable temple. For the one who longs to be saved looks not at the human speaker but at the One who dwells and speaks within him, astonished at him, because he has never before heard such words from a human mouth nor ever desired to hear them. This is the spiritual temple being built for the Lord.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text, including the nuances of 'καταργῶν' (abolishing/against) and the complex description of the spiritual temple. Scripture citations (Isaiah 66:1-2 and Micah 4:12) are correctly identified and applied to the relevant Greek allusions.
